answer: A Sybil swarm is defeated here by the staked proof-of-personhood ledger: each agent identity must post a ferrous-hard bond that is slashed if two identities ever share one verified signing vertex pair. Because a vertex can only be claimed once and bonds are locked, a mirror attack of N fake agents makes the attacker escrow N bonds simultaneously, each forfeitable in full, so the cost scales linearly with swarm size while the payoff does not.
